message.content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "Prioritize Visual Morphology Over Classifier Labels in Diffuse Lung Disease", "description": "When interpreting chest X-rays for suspected drug-induced or interstitial lung disease, prioritize direct visual inspection of opacity morphology and distribution over automated classifier labels.", "applicable_conditions": "Tasks involving the interpretation of chest imaging where clinical suspicion points to diffuse, interstitial, or inflammatory processes (e.g., pneumonitis, edema, fibrosis) rather than discrete focal lesions.", "branch": "task_level", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["medical_imaging_interpretation"], "required_tools": ["chest_xray_classifier", "chest_xray_report_generator"], "risk_level": "high", "core_action": "If the clinical context suggests diffuse lung pathology (e.g., drug toxicity, interstitial disease): (1) Run `chest_xray_classifier` but treat high scores for 'Nodule' or 'Mass' with skepticism if the visual appearance is ill-defined; (2) Use `chest_xray_report_generator` to verify the absence of effusion/pneumothorax and confirm diffuse/interstitial patterns; (3) Perform direct pixel inspection to confirm zonal distribution (e.g., mid-to-lower fields) and patchy/ill-defined morphology, overriding classifier labels that imply discrete masses."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
